{"content":"## Revolut Product Launches — 2024 & 2025

### 2024

- **eSIM (March 2024)** — Revolut became one of the first digital banks in the EEA to offer eSIMs, providing global data plans in 100+ countries directly from the app. Available to all customers on eSIM-compatible devices, with data allowances included for Premium, Metal, and Ultra plans.

- **AI-based scam detection (February 2024)** — Launched an AI-powered feature to detect and prevent scams for customers.

- **Revolut X crypto exchange (May 2024)** — A standalone desktop crypto exchange targeting experienced traders, offering 100+ tokens with 0% maker fees and 0.09% taker fees. Integrated with the main Revolut app for seamless fiat-to-crypto on/off-ramping.

- **Fiat-to-crypto on-ramp for MetaMask (March 2024)** — Partnership enabling MetaMask wallet users to purchase crypto directly via Revolut.

- **Point-of-Sale (POS) product (2024)** — Launched a merchant POS system for businesses, entering direct competition with Square and iZettle, with features including low transaction fees and 24-hour settlement.

- **Pay Later / BNPL (2024)** — Rolled out a "Pay Later" instalment product in Ireland, allowing customers to spread purchases over three instalments with affordability and suitability checks.

- **Personal loans in Italy (2024)** — Launched a personal loan product for Italian customers.

- **Charity Donations feature (2024)** — Introduced an in-app charity donations feature.

- **Wealth protection feature (2024)** — Launched a wealth protection tool for customers.

- **Four new Metal card colours (2024)** — Expanded the Metal card range with new colour options.

### 2025

- **AI-powered financial assistant (phased rollout from 2025)** — An AI assistant designed to offer personalised financial advice, automate administrative tasks, and adapt to individual user needs. Announced at the "Revolutionaries" event in London in late 2024 for 2025 rollout.

- **Branded ATMs (starting in Spain, 2025)** — Revolut-branded ATMs featuring advanced security measures such as facial recognition and cash deposit capabilities.

- **Revolut Business credit product in Europe (2025)** — First credit product for business customers in EU markets, alongside competitive business savings rates.

- **Digital mortgages** — Made available in Lithuania, Ireland, and France.

- **Stablecoin conversions (late 2024/2025)** — Fee-free USD/stablecoin conversions (USDT and USDC at 1:1 rate), with a GBP stablecoin entering the FCA regulatory sandbox.

- **Lightspark / Lightning Network integration (May 2025)** — Partnership with Lightspark to enable near-instant Bitcoin transactions in Europe and the UK via the Lightning Network.

- **Trust Wallet integration (2025)** — Integration with Trust Wallet to facilitate crypto purchases for European users.

- **Revolut Kiosk with biometric payments (2025)** — Tools for retail and restaurant operations, including biometric payment capabilities.

- **Revolut Pay platform expansion (2025)** — Integrated multiple payment methods including Buy Now Pay Later options.

- **Street Mode security feature (2025)** — An in-app feature to combat "transfer mugging" by limiting what can be accessed when the phone is unlocked in public.

- **In-app calls for scam prevention (January 2025)** — Feature to combat impersonation scams by enabling verified in-app calls.

- **Mexico bank launch (October 2025)** — Revolut became the first independent digital bank to receive full regulatory approval in Mexico through a direct application, capitalised with over $100 million.

- **Expanded crypto exchange (250+ tokens, MiCA-licensed)** — Revolut X expanded to 250+ tokens across the EEA under a MiCA crypto-asset service provider licence obtained in 2025.

### Key milestones alongside product launches

- Reached **50 million global customers** in 2024 and **75 million+** by mid-2026.
- **$45 billion valuation** (August 2024), rising to **$75 billion** (November 2025).
- **$3.8 billion revenue** in 2024; **$6 billion revenue** in 2025.
- Secured **full UK banking licence** (March 2026).

## Revolut Product Launches — 2024 & 2025

### 2024

- **eSIM (March 2024)** — Revolut became one of the first digital banks in the EEA to offer eSIMs, providing global data plans in 100+ countries directly from the app. Available to all customers on eSIM-compatible devices, with data allowances included for Premium, Metal, and Ultra plans.

- **AI-based scam detection (February 2024)** — Launched an AI-powered feature to detect and prevent scams for customers.

- **Revolut X crypto exchange (May 2024)** — A standalone desktop crypto exchange targeting experienced traders, offering 100+ tokens with 0% maker fees and 0.09% taker fees. Integrated with the main Revolut app for seamless fiat-to-crypto on/off-ramping.

- **Fiat-to-crypto on-ramp for MetaMask (March 2024)** — Partnership enabling MetaMask wallet users to purchase crypto directly via Revolut.

- **Point-of-Sale (POS) product (2024)** — Launched a merchant POS system for businesses, entering direct competition with Square and iZettle, with features including low transaction fees and 24-hour settlement.

- **Pay Later / BNPL (2024)** — Rolled out a "Pay Later" instalment product in Ireland, allowing customers to spread purchases over three instalments with affordability and suitability checks.

- **Personal loans in Italy (2024)** — Launched a personal loan product for Italian customers.

- **Charity Donations feature (2024)** — Introduced an in-app charity donations feature.

- **Wealth protection feature (2024)** — Launched a wealth protection tool for customers.

- **Four new Metal card colours (2024)** — Expanded the Metal card range with new colour options.

### 2025

- **AI-powered financial assistant (phased rollout from 2025)** — An AI assistant designed to offer personalised financial advice, automate administrative tasks, and adapt to individual user needs. Announced at the "Revolutionaries" event in London in late 2024 for 2025 rollout.

- **Branded ATMs (starting in Spain, 2025)** — Revolut-branded ATMs featuring advanced security measures such as facial recognition and cash deposit capabilities.

- **Revolut Business credit product in Europe (2025)** — First credit product for business customers in EU markets, alongside competitive business savings rates.

- **Digital mortgages** — Made available in Lithuania, Ireland, and France.

- **Stablecoin conversions (late 2024/2025)** — Fee-free USD/stablecoin conversions (USDT and USDC at 1:1 rate), with a GBP stablecoin entering the FCA regulatory sandbox.

- **Lightspark / Lightning Network integration (May 2025)** — Partnership with Lightspark to enable near-instant Bitcoin transactions in Europe and the UK via the Lightning Network.

- **Trust Wallet integration (2025)** — Integration with Trust Wallet to facilitate crypto purchases for European users.

- **Revolut Kiosk with biometric payments (2025)** — Tools for retail and restaurant operations, including biometric payment capabilities.

- **Revolut Pay platform expansion (2025)** — Integrated multiple payment methods including Buy Now Pay Later options.

- **Street Mode security feature (2025)** — An in-app feature to combat "transfer mugging" by limiting what can be accessed when the phone is unlocked in public.

- **In-app calls for scam prevention (January 2025)** — Feature to combat impersonation scams by enabling verified in-app calls.

- **Mexico bank launch (October 2025)** — Revolut became the first independent digital bank to receive full regulatory approval in Mexico through a direct application, capitalised with over $100 million.

- **Expanded crypto exchange (250+ tokens, MiCA-licensed)** — Revolut X expanded to 250+ tokens across the EEA under a MiCA crypto-asset service provider licence obtained in 2025.

### Key milestones alongside product launches

- Reached **50 million global customers** in 2024 and **75 million+** by mid-2026.
- **$45 billion valuation** (August 2024), rising to **$75 billion** (November 2025).
- **$3.8 billion revenue** in 2024; **$6 billion revenue** in 2025.
- Secured **full UK banking licence** (March 2026).

Revolut has announced a comprehensive range of new products and features in 2024 and 2025, demonstrating significant innovation across digital banking, crypto, security, and business services.

## 2024 Product Launches

**Digital Banking & Payments:**
- **eSIM (March 2024)**: Revolut became one of the first digital banks in the EEA to offer eSIMs, providing global data plans in 100+ countries directly from the app, with data allowances included for Premium, Metal, and Ultra plans.
- **Point-of-Sale (POS) product**: Launched a merchant POS system for businesses with low transaction fees and 24-hour settlement, competing directly with Square and iZettle.
- **Pay Later / BNPL**: Rolled out a "Pay Later" instalment product in Ireland, allowing customers to spread purchases over three instalments with affordability and suitability checks.
- **Personal loans in Italy**: Launched a personal loan product for Italian customers.
- **Four new Metal card colours**: Expanded the Metal card range with new colour options.

**Crypto & Trading:**
- **Revolut X crypto exchange (May 2024)**: A standalone desktop crypto exchange targeting experienced traders, offering 100+ tokens with 0% maker fees and 0.09% taker fees, integrated with the main Revolut app for seamless fiat-to-crypto on/off-ramping.
- **Fiat-to-crypto on-ramp for MetaMask (March 2024)**: Partnership enabling MetaMask wallet users to purchase crypto directly via Revolut.

**Security & Protection:**
- **AI-based scam detection (February 2024)**: Launched an AI-powered feature to detect and prevent scams for customers.
- **Wealth protection feature**: Launched a wealth protection tool for customers.
- **Charity Donations feature**: Introduced an in-app charity donations feature.

## 2025 Product Launches & Announcements

**AI & Innovation:**
- **AI-powered financial assistant (phased rollout from 2025)**: An AI assistant designed to offer personalised financial advice, automate administrative tasks, and adapt to individual user needs, announced at the "Revolutionaries" event in London.
- **Branded ATMs (starting in Spain, 2025)**: Revolut-branded ATMs featuring advanced security measures such as facial recognition and cash deposit capabilities.

**Business Products:**
- **Revolut Business credit product in Europe (2025)**: First credit product for business customers in EU markets, alongside competitive business savings rates.
- **Revolut Kiosk with biometric payments (2025)**: Tools for retail and restaurant operations, including biometric payment capabilities.
- **Revolut Pay platform expansion (2025)**: Integrated multiple payment methods including Buy Now Pay Later options.

**Lending & Mortgages:**
- **Digital mortgages**: Made available in Lithuania, Ireland, and France.

**Crypto Expansion:**
- **Stablecoin conversions (late 2024/2025)**: Fee-free USD/stablecoin conversions (USDT and USDC at 1:1 rate), with a GBP stablecoin entering the FCA regulatory sandbox.
- **Lightspark / Lightning Network integration (May 2025)**: Partnership with Lightspark to enable near-instant Bitcoin transactions in Europe and the UK via the Lightning Network.
- **Trust Wallet integration (2025)**: Integration with Trust Wallet to facilitate crypto purchases for European users.
- **Expanded crypto exchange (250+ tokens, MiCA-licensed)**: Revolut X expanded to 250+ tokens across the EEA under a MiCA crypto-asset service provider licence obtained in 2025.

**Security Features:**
- **Street Mode security feature (2025)**: An in-app feature to combat "transfer mugging" by limiting what can be accessed when the phone is unlocked in public.
- **In-app calls for scam prevention (January 2025)**: Feature to combat impersonation scams by enabling verified in-app calls.

**Geographic Expansion:**
- **Mexico bank launch (October 2025)**: Revolut became the first independent digital bank to receive full regulatory approval in Mexico through a direct application, capitalised with over $100 million.

These launches coincide with significant business milestones, including reaching 50 million global customers in 2024 and 75 million+ by mid-2026, achieving a $45 billion valuation in August 2024 (rising to $75 billion in November 2025), and securing a full UK banking licence in March 2026.

query: What do users value and complain about in the competitor's (Revolut) app reviews?
answer:
Based on app reviews and customer feedback, Revolut users value and complain about the following aspects:

## What Users Value

**User-Friendly Interface**: Customers consistently praise the intuitive design and ease of navigation, making everyday financial management straightforward and stress-free.

**Competitive Exchange Rates**: One of the most-cited benefits is the ability to spend and send money abroad at favorable rates, with users highlighting significant savings on international transactions. The app allows holding up to 36 currencies and spending in 150+ currencies.

**Speed of Transactions**: Fast money transfers are frequently mentioned as a standout feature, including the ability to receive salary a day early.

**All-in-One Financial App**: Users appreciate having multiple services consolidated in a single app, including payments, savings, investments, crypto, insurance, and budgeting tools.

**Multi-Currency Support**: The ability to hold multiple currencies and spend globally is highly valued, especially by travelers and expats.

**Security Features**: 24/7 account protection, virtual cards, and single-use virtual cards for extra safety receive positive feedback from users.

The app holds a 4.9/5 rating on the UK App Store (with 1.1 million reviews as of August 2026) and an average 4.7/5 on Trustpilot, and was awarded World's Best Digital Bank 2025 by Euromoney.

## Common User Complaints

**Customer Support Delays**: This is the most recurring complaint. Users report slow response times, especially for complex or urgent issues. Support is primarily via in-app chat, and some users find it difficult to reach a human agent quickly. Premium/Metal subscribers get priority support, but free-tier users often experience longer wait times.

**Account Freezes and Restrictions**: A significant source of frustration. Accounts can be frozen or restricted—sometimes without clear prior warning—due to compliance checks (KYC/AML). Users report difficulty accessing their funds during these periods and slow resolution times.

**Fraud and Scam Complaint Handling**: Revolut has been flagged as having the highest number of fraud and scam complaints escalated to the UK Financial Ombudsman Service (FOS). In 2024, it recorded the most authorized push payment (APP) fraud complaints among UK firms and led in non-APP fraud/scam complaints (2,631 in 2024), with a 37% uphold rate for non-APP cases—meaning the ombudsman sided with the customer in over a third of cases.

**Unexpected Fees**: Some users report encountering charges they didn't anticipate, particularly around currency exchange outside of market hours or exceeding free-tier limits.

**Account Closure Without Clear Explanation**: Business and personal users alike have reported sudden account closures tied to compliance or risk classification, with limited transparency on the reasons.

## Overall Sentiment

The overall sentiment is strongly positive, with users valuing Revolut's speed, low-cost international capabilities, and feature-rich app. However, customer support responsiveness, account freezing/restriction practices, and fraud complaint handling remain the primary pain points. Many experts recommend using Revolut as a supplementary bank for travel and special features, while noting that reliance on it as a sole primary bank carries some risk due to potential complications with account access.

## Revolut App: User Reviews, Complaints & What Users Value

Revolut is a London-based fintech and digital banking company founded in 2013, now trusted by over 75–80 million customers worldwide. As of August 2026, the app holds a **4.9/5 rating** on the App Store (UK, 1.1 million reviews) and an average **4.7/5 on Trustpilot**. It was also awarded **World's Best Digital Bank 2025** by Euromoney.

---

### What Users Value Most

- **User-friendly interface:** Customers consistently praise the intuitive design and ease of navigation, making everyday financial management straightforward.
- **Competitive exchange rates:** Spending and sending money abroad at favourable rates is one of the most-cited benefits. Users highlight savings on international transactions.
- **Speed of transactions:** Fast money transfers — including receiving salary a day early — are frequently mentioned as a standout feature.
- **All-in-one financial app:** Users appreciate having multiple services (payments, savings, investments, crypto, insurance, budgeting) consolidated in a single app.
- **Multi-currency support:** Holding up to 36 currencies and spending in 150+ currencies is highly valued, especially by travellers and expats.
- **Security features:** 24/7 account protection, virtual cards, and single-use virtual cards for extra safety are noted positively.

---

### Common User Complaints

- **Customer support delays:** This is the most recurring complaint. Users report slow response times, especially for complex or urgent issues. Support is primarily via in-app chat, and some users find it difficult to reach a human agent quickly. Premium/Metal subscribers get priority, but free-tier users often experience longer waits.
- **Account freezes and restrictions:** A significant source of frustration. Accounts can be frozen or restricted — sometimes without clear prior warning — due to compliance checks (KYC/AML). Users report difficulty accessing their funds during these periods and slow resolution.
- **Fraud and scam complaint handling:** Revolut has been flagged as having the highest number of fraud and scam complaints escalated to the UK Financial Ombudsman Service (FOS). In 2024, it recorded the most authorised push payment (APP) fraud complaints among UK firms, and also led in non-APP fraud/scam complaints (2,631 in 2024), with a 37% uphold rate for non-APP cases — meaning the ombudsman sided with the customer in over a third of cases.
- **Unexpected fees:** Some users report encountering charges they didn't anticipate, particularly around currency exchange outside of market hours or exceeding free-tier limits.
- **Account closure without clear explanation:** Business and personal users alike have reported sudden account closures tied to compliance or risk classification, with limited transparency on the reasons.

---

### Summary

Overall sentiment is **strongly positive**, with users valuing Revolut's speed, low-cost international capabilities, and feature-rich app. However, **customer support responsiveness**, **account freezing/restriction practices**, and **fraud complaint handling** remain the primary pain points. Many experts recommend using Revolut as a supplementary bank for travel and special features, while noting that reliance on it as a sole primary bank carries some risk due to potential complications with account access.

input.answer:
Based on app reviews and customer feedback, Revolut users value and complain about the following aspects:

## What Users Value

**User-Friendly Interface**: Customers consistently praise the intuitive design and ease of navigation, making everyday financial management straightforward and stress-free.

**Competitive Exchange Rates**: One of the most-cited benefits is the ability to spend and send money abroad at favorable rates, with users highlighting significant savings on international transactions. The app allows holding up to 36 currencies and spending in 150+ currencies.

**Speed of Transactions**: Fast money transfers are frequently mentioned as a standout feature, including the ability to receive salary a day early.

**All-in-One Financial App**: Users appreciate having multiple services consolidated in a single app, including payments, savings, investments, crypto, insurance, and budgeting tools.

**Multi-Currency Support**: The ability to hold multiple currencies and spend globally is highly valued, especially by travelers and expats.

**Security Features**: 24/7 account protection, virtual cards, and single-use virtual cards for extra safety receive positive feedback from users.

The app holds a 4.9/5 rating on the UK App Store (with 1.1 million reviews as of August 2026) and an average 4.7/5 on Trustpilot, and was awarded World's Best Digital Bank 2025 by Euromoney.

## Common User Complaints

**Customer Support Delays**: This is the most recurring complaint. Users report slow response times, especially for complex or urgent issues. Support is primarily via in-app chat, and some users find it difficult to reach a human agent quickly. Premium/Metal subscribers get priority support, but free-tier users often experience longer wait times.

**Account Freezes and Restrictions**: A significant source of frustration. Accounts can be frozen or restricted—sometimes without clear prior warning—due to compliance checks (KYC/AML). Users report difficulty accessing their funds during these periods and slow resolution times.

**Fraud and Scam Complaint Handling**: Revolut has been flagged as having the highest number of fraud and scam complaints escalated to the UK Financial Ombudsman Service (FOS). In 2024, it recorded the most authorized push payment (APP) fraud complaints among UK firms and led in non-APP fraud/scam complaints (2,631 in 2024), with a 37% uphold rate for non-APP cases—meaning the ombudsman sided with the customer in over a third of cases.

**Unexpected Fees**: Some users report encountering charges they didn't anticipate, particularly around currency exchange outside of market hours or exceeding free-tier limits.

**Account Closure Without Clear Explanation**: Business and personal users alike have reported sudden account closures tied to compliance or risk classification, with limited transparency on the reasons.

## Overall Sentiment

The overall sentiment is strongly positive, with users valuing Revolut's speed, low-cost international capabilities, and feature-rich app. However, customer support responsiveness, account freezing/restriction practices, and fraud complaint handling remain the primary pain points. Many experts recommend using Revolut as a supplementary bank for travel and special features, while noting that reliance on it as a sole primary bank carries some risk due to potential complications with account access.

answer:
BBVA, the Spanish multinational banking and financial services company, publishes comprehensive profiles and requirements for senior leadership positions through its formal governance policies and corporate documentation. Here's what BBVA publicly discloses about leadership role requirements:

## **Formal Selection Policy for Board Directors and Senior Leadership**

BBVA maintains a **"Policy on the Selection, Suitability and Diversity of the Board of Directors"** that establishes clear criteria for leadership positions:

### **1. Legal & Regulatory Suitability Requirements**

All directors and senior executives must meet:
- **Recognized commercial and professional reputation**
- **Adequate knowledge and experience** to discharge their duties
- **Ability to exercise good governance** of the entity
- Registration with the **Registry of Senior Banking Officers of the Bank of Spain** (for executive directors)
- Compliance with **due diligence and loyalty duties**, avoidance of conflicts of interest, and adherence to incompatibility and limitations regimes

### **2. Professional & Academic Qualifications**

BBVA requires directors to have:
- **Extensive training and experience**, both nationally and internationally, in areas including:
  - Banking and finance
  - Accounting and risk management
  - Law
  - Academia
  - Technology
  - Sustainability and climate change
- Professional experience of a **sufficient level and standard**, particularly in banking and financial services
- **Practical experience** from previous positions held for sufficient periods of time
- **Sufficient availability and dedication** to carry out duties, including committee membership responsibilities

### **3. Key Competencies & Skills Matrix**

BBVA uses a **"skills and diversity matrix"** to assess collective competencies of board members and senior leaders. Key competency areas include:

- **Financial sector expertise** — deep knowledge of banking, credit, treasury, and international business
- **Risk management and auditing** — solid expertise in identifying and managing financial and operational risks
- **Strategic and operational leadership** — experience leading large, complex organizations
- **Digital transformation** — understanding of technology and innovation in financial services (BBVA has extended its OpenAI partnership across its 120,000-employee workforce)
- **Sustainability and ESG** — expertise in climate change, environmental policy, and responsible banking
- **Regulatory and governance knowledge** — familiarity with banking regulation and corporate governance frameworks
- **International exposure** — experience across key geographic markets relevant to BBVA (Spain, Mexico, Turkey, South America, and other markets)

### **4. Board Composition & Diversity Objectives**

BBVA's published diversity targets for leadership include:

- **Independence**: At least **50% independent directors** (currently exceeding this with 10 out of 15 members being independent)
- **Gender diversity**: Approximately **47% women** on the Board (7 out of 15 members), with a target of **36.8% female managers** by end of 2026
- **Non-executive majority**: 13 out of 15 board members are non-executive
- **Diversity of profiles**: Inclusion based on gender, academic background, professional experience, knowledge, disability, origin, and age
- Application of the **Rooney Rule** internally, requiring at least half of final candidates for internal positions to be women (resulting in 52% of promotions going to women)

### **5. Selection & Evaluation Process**

BBVA's **Appointments and Corporate Governance Committee** is responsible for:
- Evaluating candidates against qualification criteria
- Assessing each candidate's suitability, including skills, experience, merits, and knowledge
- Considering current and future needs of the Board, structure and size, and term expiries
- Taking into account opinions from shareholders, investors, proxy advisors, supervisory authorities, and other stakeholders
- Verifying ongoing suitability on each renewal or re-election

### **6. Remuneration & Governance Framework**

For senior management and "Identified Staff" (individuals whose professional activities may significantly impact the entity's risk profile):
- Contractual clauses cover duration, notice periods, hiring bonuses, and indemnities for early termination
- Remuneration follows **Bank of Spain Circular 2/2016** regulations
- Long-term variable incentives for executive directors and senior management are tied to diversity metrics (e.g., evolution of women in management positions accounts for 5% of long-term variable remuneration)

### **7. Current Leadership Structure**

BBVA's published senior leadership includes:
- **Executive Chairman**: Carlos Torres Vila
- **CEO**: Onur Genç
- **CFO**: Gonzalo Rodríguez Rodríguez
- **CCO (Chief Compliance Officer)**: Rocío Pérez Mies
- **CRO (Chief Risk Officer)**: Pablo Pastor / José Luis Elechiguerra
- **Country Manager, BBVA Spain**: Cristina de Parias
- **Global Head of Talent & Culture**: Paul G. Tobin

### **8. Career Opportunities & Recruitment**

BBVA emphasizes talent and culture as strategic priorities:
- Career opportunities are posted on **bbva.com** and through dedicated careers channels
- The bank offers global mobility across Spain, Latin America, Turkey, the US, and Asia
- Focus on innovation, digital banking, AI, and fintech attracts professionals in these fields
- BBVA was recognized among the **10 best companies in the world** by Time magazine's "World's Best Companies 2025"

These published requirements demonstrate BBVA's commitment to transparency in leadership selection, with clear emphasis on professional qualifications, diversity, regulatory compliance, and alignment with the bank's digital transformation and sustainability strategies.

{"content":"## BBVA — Leadership Roles and Senior Positions

### Overview

BBVA (Banco Bilbao Vizcaya Argentaria) is a Spanish multinational banking and financial services company headquartered in Bilbao, founded in 1857. Below is a summary of its key leadership roles, senior executive profiles, and related governance requirements.

---

### Key Senior Leadership Positions

| Role | Name |
|------|------|
| **Executive Chairman** | Carlos Torres Vila |
| **CEO** | Onur Genç |
| **CFO** | Gonzalo Rodríguez Rodríguez |
| **CCO (Chief Compliance Officer)** | Rocío Pérez Mies |
| **CRO (Chief Risk Officer)** | Pablo Pastor / José Luis Elechiguerra |
| **Country Manager, BBVA Spain** | Cristina de Parias |

In July 2026, BBVA reshuffled its leadership team, naming a new CFO and Mexico head as part of a broader executive reorganization.

---

### Board & Governance Requirements

BBVA's corporate governance framework sets specific requirements for senior positions, including:

- **Board Committees**: The bank operates an Audit Committee, a Nomination and Remuneration Committee, and other specialized committees that oversee executive appointments.
- **Remuneration of senior management**: Contractual clauses for executive directors cover duration, notice periods, hiring bonuses, and indemnities in the event of early termination.
- **Identified Staff**: BBVA follows Bank of Spain regulations (including Circular 2/2016) regarding remuneration and governance for individuals whose professional activities may have a significant impact on the entity's risk profile.

---

### Diversity in Leadership

- BBVA surpassed **35% women in leadership roles** as of early 2025.
- The bank raised its target to **36.8% female managers by end of 2026**, with this indicator tied to long-term variable incentives for executive directors and senior management.
- The **Rooney Rule** is applied internally, requiring that at least half of final candidates for internal positions be women. As a result, 52% of promotions went to women in recent years.
- The **BBVA Tech Woman** program has boosted women in STEM fields to 30.6%.

---

### Notable Recent Departures

- **Alfonso Gómez**, a 31-year BBVA veteran and former Swiss chief, departed in April 2026 to become CEO of HSBC Swiss Private Bank.

---

### Profile Requirements for Senior Roles

Senior leadership at BBVA typically requires:
- Deep expertise in banking, financial services, or technology
- Significant international experience (BBVA operates across Spain, Mexico, Turkey, South America, and other markets)
- Alignment with the bank's digital transformation and AI strategy (e.g., the bank has extended its OpenAI partnership to embed AI across its 120,000-employee workforce)
- Compliance with regulatory fitness and propriety standards set by the European Central Bank and Bank of Spain

## BBVA — Leadership Roles and Senior Positions

### Overview

BBVA (Banco Bilbao Vizcaya Argentaria) is a Spanish multinational banking and financial services company headquartered in Bilbao, founded in 1857. Below is a summary of its key leadership roles, senior executive profiles, and related governance requirements.

---

### Key Senior Leadership Positions

| Role | Name |
|------|------|
| **Executive Chairman** | Carlos Torres Vila |
| **CEO** | Onur Genç |
| **CFO** | Gonzalo Rodríguez Rodríguez |
| **CCO (Chief Compliance Officer)** | Rocío Pérez Mies |
| **CRO (Chief Risk Officer)** | Pablo Pastor / José Luis Elechiguerra |
| **Country Manager, BBVA Spain** | Cristina de Parias |

In July 2026, BBVA reshuffled its leadership team, naming a new CFO and Mexico head as part of a broader executive reorganization.

---

### Board & Governance Requirements

BBVA's corporate governance framework sets specific requirements for senior positions, including:

- **Board Committees**: The bank operates an Audit Committee, a Nomination and Remuneration Committee, and other specialized committees that oversee executive appointments.
- **Remuneration of senior management**: Contractual clauses for executive directors cover duration, notice periods, hiring bonuses, and indemnities in the event of early termination.
- **Identified Staff**: BBVA follows Bank of Spain regulations (including Circular 2/2016) regarding remuneration and governance for individuals whose professional activities may have a significant impact on the entity's risk profile.

---

### Diversity in Leadership

- BBVA surpassed **35% women in leadership roles** as of early 2025.
- The bank raised its target to **36.8% female managers by end of 2026**, with this indicator tied to long-term variable incentives for executive directors and senior management.
- The **Rooney Rule** is applied internally, requiring that at least half of final candidates for internal positions be women. As a result, 52% of promotions went to women in recent years.
- The **BBVA Tech Woman** program has boosted women in STEM fields to 30.6%.

---

### Notable Recent Departures

- **Alfonso Gómez**, a 31-year BBVA veteran and former Swiss chief, departed in April 2026 to become CEO of HSBC Swiss Private Bank.

---

### Profile Requirements for Senior Roles

Senior leadership at BBVA typically requires:
- Deep expertise in banking, financial services, or technology
- Significant international experience (BBVA operates across Spain, Mexico, Turkey, South America, and other markets)
- Alignment with the bank's digital transformation and AI strategy (e.g., the bank has extended its OpenAI partnership to embed AI across its 120,000-employee workforce)
- Compliance with regulatory fitness and propriety standards set by the European Central Bank and Bank of Spain

{"content":"# BBVA Board of Directors — Leadership Qualifications, Competencies & Selection Criteria

BBVA (Banco Bilbao Vizcaya Argentaria) is a Spanish multinational banking and financial services company headquartered in Bilbao, founded in 1857. The bank maintains a formal **Policy on the Selection, Suitability and Diversity of the Board of Directors** that governs how directors and executive leaders are chosen. Below is a summary of the key requirements and competencies.

---

## 1. Legal & Regulatory Suitability Requirements

BBVA directors must comply with all legal requirements necessary to perform the role under applicable regulations, including:

- **Recognised commercial and professional repute**
- **Adequate knowledge and experience** to discharge their duties
- **Ability to exercise good governance** of the entity
- Registration with the **Registry of Senior Banking Officers of the Bank of Spain** (for executive directors)
- Compliance with **due diligence and loyalty duties**, avoidance of conflicts of interest, and adherence to the incompatibility and limitations regime set out in applicable regulations

---

## 2. Professional & Academic Qualifications

Directors must have:

- **Extensive training and experience**, both nationally and internationally, in areas such as:
  - Banking and finance
  - Accounting and risk management
  - Law
  - Academia
  - Technology
  - Sustainability and climate change
- Professional experience of a **sufficient level and standard**, particularly in banking and financial services
- **Practical experience** from previous positions held for sufficient periods of time

---

## 3. Key Competencies & Skills

The Board uses a **"skills and diversity matrix"** to assess the collective competencies of its members. Key competency areas include:

- **Financial sector expertise** — deep knowledge of banking, credit, treasury, and international business
- **Risk management and auditing** — solid expertise in identifying and managing financial and operational risks
- **Strategic and operational leadership** — experience leading large, complex organizations
- **Digital transformation** — understanding of technology and innovation in financial services
- **Sustainability and ESG** — expertise in climate change, environmental policy, and responsible banking
- **Regulatory and governance knowledge** — familiarity with banking regulation and corporate governance frameworks
- **International exposure** — experience across key geographic markets relevant to BBVA

---

## 4. Board Composition & Diversity Objectives

BBVA's selection policy promotes diversity across multiple dimensions:

- **Independence**: The Board targets at least **50% independent directors** (currently exceeding this, with 10 out of 15 members being independent)
- **Gender diversity**: The Board has progressively increased female representation, reaching approximately **47% women** (7 out of 15 members)
- **Diversity of profiles**: The policy encourages inclusion of people with different profiles based on gender, academic background, professional experience, knowledge, disability, origin, and age
- **Non-executive majority**: A broad majority of non-executive directors (13 out of 15)
- Only **three executive directors** on the Board

---

## 5. Selection & Evaluation Process

- The **Appointments and Corporate Governance Committee** is responsible for evaluating candidates against the qualification criteria
- The Committee assesses each candidate's suitability, including skills, experience, merits, and knowledge
- It considers the **current and future needs** of the Board, the structure and size of the Board, and the expiry of directors' terms
- The Committee takes into account opinions from **shareholders, investors, proxy advisors, supervisory authorities, and other stakeholders**
- Candidates must demonstrate **sufficient availability and dedication** to carry out their duties, including committee membership responsibilities

---

## 6. Ongoing Suitability Verification

BBVA's Board continuously verifies the suitability of its directors by applying the requirements set out in current legislation. On each renewal or re-election, the Appointments Committee confirms that no circumstances have arisen that would change the director's suitability assessment.

# BBVA Board of Directors — Leadership Qualifications, Competencies & Selection Criteria

BBVA (Banco Bilbao Vizcaya Argentaria) is a Spanish multinational banking and financial services company headquartered in Bilbao, founded in 1857. The bank maintains a formal **Policy on the Selection, Suitability and Diversity of the Board of Directors** that governs how directors and executive leaders are chosen. Below is a summary of the key requirements and competencies.

---

## 1. Legal & Regulatory Suitability Requirements

BBVA directors must comply with all legal requirements necessary to perform the role under applicable regulations, including:

- **Recognised commercial and professional repute**
- **Adequate knowledge and experience** to discharge their duties
- **Ability to exercise good governance** of the entity
- Registration with the **Registry of Senior Banking Officers of the Bank of Spain** (for executive directors)
- Compliance with **due diligence and loyalty duties**, avoidance of conflicts of interest, and adherence to the incompatibility and limitations regime set out in applicable regulations

---

## 2. Professional & Academic Qualifications

Directors must have:

- **Extensive training and experience**, both nationally and internationally, in areas such as:
  - Banking and finance
  - Accounting and risk management
  - Law
  - Academia
  - Technology
  - Sustainability and climate change
- Professional experience of a **sufficient level and standard**, particularly in banking and financial services
- **Practical experience** from previous positions held for sufficient periods of time

---

## 3. Key Competencies & Skills

The Board uses a **"skills and diversity matrix"** to assess the collective competencies of its members. Key competency areas include:

- **Financial sector expertise** — deep knowledge of banking, credit, treasury, and international business
- **Risk management and auditing** — solid expertise in identifying and managing financial and operational risks
- **Strategic and operational leadership** — experience leading large, complex organizations
- **Digital transformation** — understanding of technology and innovation in financial services
- **Sustainability and ESG** — expertise in climate change, environmental policy, and responsible banking
- **Regulatory and governance knowledge** — familiarity with banking regulation and corporate governance frameworks
- **International exposure** — experience across key geographic markets relevant to BBVA

---

## 4. Board Composition & Diversity Objectives

BBVA's selection policy promotes diversity across multiple dimensions:

- **Independence**: The Board targets at least **50% independent directors** (currently exceeding this, with 10 out of 15 members being independent)
- **Gender diversity**: The Board has progressively increased female representation, reaching approximately **47% women** (7 out of 15 members)
- **Diversity of profiles**: The policy encourages inclusion of people with different profiles based on gender, academic background, professional experience, knowledge, disability, origin, and age
- **Non-executive majority**: A broad majority of non-executive directors (13 out of 15)
- Only **three executive directors** on the Board

---

## 5. Selection & Evaluation Process

- The **Appointments and Corporate Governance Committee** is responsible for evaluating candidates against the qualification criteria
- The Committee assesses each candidate's suitability, including skills, experience, merits, and knowledge
- It considers the **current and future needs** of the Board, the structure and size of the Board, and the expiry of directors' terms
- The Committee takes into account opinions from **shareholders, investors, proxy advisors, supervisory authorities, and other stakeholders**
- Candidates must demonstrate **sufficient availability and dedication** to carry out their duties, including committee membership responsibilities

---

## 6. Ongoing Suitability Verification

BBVA's Board continuously verifies the suitability of its directors by applying the requirements set out in current legislation. On each renewal or re-election, the Appointments Committee confirms that no circumstances have arisen that would change the director's suitability assessment.

Directors must be registered with the Registry of Senior Banking Officers of the Bank of Spain when they are executive directors, as shown by the suitability reports for executive members.

The policy demands extensive professional and academic training in banking, finance, accounting, risk, law, technology, sustainability and related fields, ensuring a sufficient level and standard of experience.

A “skills and diversity matrix” is used to assess collective competencies, covering financial sector expertise, risk management, strategic leadership, digital transformation, ESG, regulatory knowledge and international exposure.
The Board targets at least 50 % independent directors and currently exceeds this target with 10 independent members out of 15, confirming the independence requirement.
Gender diversity is pursued, with women representing roughly 47 % of the Board (7 out of 15), reflecting the policy’s emphasis on gender balance.
The composition aims for a majority of non‑executive directors (13 of 15) and limits executive directors to three, aligning with the policy’s non‑executive majority objective.
The Appointments and Corporate Governance Committee evaluates candidates against the qualification criteria, considering current and future board needs, term expiries and stakeholder input.
Ongoing suitability is verified on each renewal or re‑election, ensuring directors continue to meet legal and policy requirements.

{"content":"## BBVA — Executive Director & Senior Management: Overview, Roles, and Career Opportunities

### About BBVA

BBVA (Banco Bilbao Vizcaya Argentaria) is a Spanish multinational banking and financial services company headquartered in Bilbao, founded in 1857. It employs approximately **125,916** people worldwide and operates across multiple geographies including Spain, Latin America, Turkey, and other markets. BBVA was recognized among the **10 best companies in the world** by Time magazine's "World's Best Companies 2025" and ranked as the best bank in Spain at the sector level.

---

### Senior Management & Executive Leadership Structure

BBVA's leadership is headed by:

- **Chairman**: Carlos Torres (who reaffirmed his commitment to the bank following the conclusion of the Sabadell bid in 2025)
- **CEO**: Onur Genç
- **Global Head of Talent & Culture**: Paul G. Tobin

The executive leadership team includes Executive Directors and senior executives overseeing key areas such as:

- **Corporate & Investment Banking** — strategy, global markets, financial institutions, and sustainable finance
- **Retail Banking** — consumer banking across geographies
- **Risk Management** — Chief Risk Officers at group and regional levels (e.g., Gerardo Fiandrino served as CRO for South America)
- **Digital Transformation & Technology**
- **Talent & Culture** — responsible for recruitment, employee experience, internal communication, and senior management development
- **Communications** — e.g., Manuel Mora-Figueroa Urdiales serves as Global Head of Communications
- **Chair & CEO Office** — e.g., Matias Viola Ochoa serves as Managing Director and Front Head

---

### Executive Director Role — Typical Responsibilities

At BBVA, an Executive Director-level role in senior management typically involves:

- **Strategic leadership**: Developing and implementing strategic plans aligned with the bank's global objectives
- **Business oversight**: Managing P&L, operational performance, and regulatory compliance for a business unit or geography
- **Team leadership**: Leading and developing multidisciplinary teams, fostering a high-performance culture
- **Risk management**: Identifying and managing risks to safeguard the bank's assets and earnings
- **Stakeholder engagement**: Liaising with the board, regulators, clients, and community stakeholders
- **Financial stewardship**: Overseeing budgets, financial performance metrics, and capital allocation
- **Innovation & digital transformation**: Driving technology adoption and digital banking initiatives

---

### Career Opportunities & Talent Recruitment at BBVA

BBVA places strong emphasis on talent and culture as a strategic priority. Key highlights:

- **Careers portal**: Opportunities are posted at [bbva.com](https://www.bbva.com) and through BBVA's dedicated careers channels
- **Talent & Culture function**: Led at the executive level (e.g., at Garanti BBVA, the Executive Vice President of Talent and Culture oversees recruitment, talent solutions, remuneration, employee experience, education, and internal communication)
- **Global mobility**: BBVA offers career paths across Spain, Latin America (Mexico, Argentina, Peru, Colombia), Turkey (Garanti BBVA), the US, and Asia — with senior leaders frequently rotating across geographies
- **Innovation focus**: BBVA has been recognized for putting innovation and sustainability at the center of its strategy, making it attractive for professionals in digital banking, AI, and fintech
- **People-centric philosophy**: As Paul G. Tobin noted, BBVA's recognition reflects "the commitment and talent of everyone at BBVA" and the bank's focus on "putting people at the center"

For current openings and application details, visit BBVA's official careers page at **bbva.com**.

## BBVA — Executive Director & Senior Management: Overview, Roles, and Career Opportunities

### About BBVA

BBVA (Banco Bilbao Vizcaya Argentaria) is a Spanish multinational banking and financial services company headquartered in Bilbao, founded in 1857. It employs approximately **125,916** people worldwide and operates across multiple geographies including Spain, Latin America, Turkey, and other markets. BBVA was recognized among the **10 best companies in the world** by Time magazine's "World's Best Companies 2025" and ranked as the best bank in Spain at the sector level.

---

### Senior Management & Executive Leadership Structure

BBVA's leadership is headed by:

- **Chairman**: Carlos Torres (who reaffirmed his commitment to the bank following the conclusion of the Sabadell bid in 2025)
- **CEO**: Onur Genç
- **Global Head of Talent & Culture**: Paul G. Tobin

The executive leadership team includes Executive Directors and senior executives overseeing key areas such as:

- **Corporate & Investment Banking** — strategy, global markets, financial institutions, and sustainable finance
- **Retail Banking** — consumer banking across geographies
- **Risk Management** — Chief Risk Officers at group and regional levels (e.g., Gerardo Fiandrino served as CRO for South America)
- **Digital Transformation & Technology**
- **Talent & Culture** — responsible for recruitment, employee experience, internal communication, and senior management development
- **Communications** — e.g., Manuel Mora-Figueroa Urdiales serves as Global Head of Communications
- **Chair & CEO Office** — e.g., Matias Viola Ochoa serves as Managing Director and Front Head

---

### Executive Director Role — Typical Responsibilities

At BBVA, an Executive Director-level role in senior management typically involves:

- **Strategic leadership**: Developing and implementing strategic plans aligned with the bank's global objectives
- **Business oversight**: Managing P&L, operational performance, and regulatory compliance for a business unit or geography
- **Team leadership**: Leading and developing multidisciplinary teams, fostering a high-performance culture
- **Risk management**: Identifying and managing risks to safeguard the bank's assets and earnings
- **Stakeholder engagement**: Liaising with the board, regulators, clients, and community stakeholders
- **Financial stewardship**: Overseeing budgets, financial performance metrics, and capital allocation
- **Innovation & digital transformation**: Driving technology adoption and digital banking initiatives

---

### Career Opportunities & Talent Recruitment at BBVA

BBVA places strong emphasis on talent and culture as a strategic priority. Key highlights:

- **Careers portal**: Opportunities are posted at [bbva.com](https://www.bbva.com) and through BBVA's dedicated careers channels
- **Talent & Culture function**: Led at the executive level (e.g., at Garanti BBVA, the Executive Vice President of Talent and Culture oversees recruitment, talent solutions, remuneration, employee experience, education, and internal communication)
- **Global mobility**: BBVA offers career paths across Spain, Latin America (Mexico, Argentina, Peru, Colombia), Turkey (Garanti BBVA), the US, and Asia — with senior leaders frequently rotating across geographies
- **Innovation focus**: BBVA has been recognized for putting innovation and sustainability at the center of its strategy, making it attractive for professionals in digital banking, AI, and fintech
- **People-centric philosophy**: As Paul G. Tobin noted, BBVA's recognition reflects "the commitment and talent of everyone at BBVA" and the bank's focus on "putting people at the center"

For current openings and application details, visit BBVA's official careers page at **bbva.com**.

Talent and Culture is a strategic priority at BBVA, led by Paul G. Tobin, who emphasizes that the bank’s success reflects the commitment and talent of its people and its focus on innovation and sustainability.

BBVA, the Spanish multinational banking and financial services company, publishes comprehensive profiles and requirements for senior leadership positions through its formal governance policies and corporate documentation. Here's what BBVA publicly discloses about leadership role requirements:

## **Formal Selection Policy for Board Directors and Senior Leadership**

BBVA maintains a **"Policy on the Selection, Suitability and Diversity of the Board of Directors"** that establishes clear criteria for leadership positions:

### **1. Legal & Regulatory Suitability Requirements**

All directors and senior executives must meet:
- **Recognized commercial and professional reputation**
- **Adequate knowledge and experience** to discharge their duties
- **Ability to exercise good governance** of the entity
- Registration with the **Registry of Senior Banking Officers of the Bank of Spain** (for executive directors)
- Compliance with **due diligence and loyalty duties**, avoidance of conflicts of interest, and adherence to incompatibility and limitations regimes

### **2. Professional & Academic Qualifications**

BBVA requires directors to have:
- **Extensive training and experience**, both nationally and internationally, in areas including:
  - Banking and finance
  - Accounting and risk management
  - Law
  - Academia
  - Technology
  - Sustainability and climate change
- Professional experience of a **sufficient level and standard**, particularly in banking and financial services
- **Practical experience** from previous positions held for sufficient periods of time
- **Sufficient availability and dedication** to carry out duties, including committee membership responsibilities

### **3. Key Competencies & Skills Matrix**

BBVA uses a **"skills and diversity matrix"** to assess collective competencies of board members and senior leaders. Key competency areas include:

- **Financial sector expertise** — deep knowledge of banking, credit, treasury, and international business
- **Risk management and auditing** — solid expertise in identifying and managing financial and operational risks
- **Strategic and operational leadership** — experience leading large, complex organizations
- **Digital transformation** — understanding of technology and innovation in financial services (BBVA has extended its OpenAI partnership across its 120,000-employee workforce)
- **Sustainability and ESG** — expertise in climate change, environmental policy, and responsible banking
- **Regulatory and governance knowledge** — familiarity with banking regulation and corporate governance frameworks
- **International exposure** — experience across key geographic markets relevant to BBVA (Spain, Mexico, Turkey, South America, and other markets)

### **4. Board Composition & Diversity Objectives**

BBVA's published diversity targets for leadership include:

- **Independence**: At least **50% independent directors** (currently exceeding this with 10 out of 15 members being independent)
- **Gender diversity**: Approximately **47% women** on the Board (7 out of 15 members), with a target of **36.8% female managers** by end of 2026
- **Non-executive majority**: 13 out of 15 board members are non-executive
- **Diversity of profiles**: Inclusion based on gender, academic background, professional experience, knowledge, disability, origin, and age
- Application of the **Rooney Rule** internally, requiring at least half of final candidates for internal positions to be women (resulting in 52% of promotions going to women)

### **5. Selection & Evaluation Process**

BBVA's **Appointments and Corporate Governance Committee** is responsible for:
- Evaluating candidates against qualification criteria
- Assessing each candidate's suitability, including skills, experience, merits, and knowledge
- Considering current and future needs of the Board, structure and size, and term expiries
- Taking into account opinions from shareholders, investors, proxy advisors, supervisory authorities, and other stakeholders
- Verifying ongoing suitability on each renewal or re-election

### **6. Remuneration & Governance Framework**

For senior management and "Identified Staff" (individuals whose professional activities may significantly impact the entity's risk profile):
- Contractual clauses cover duration, notice periods, hiring bonuses, and indemnities for early termination
- Remuneration follows **Bank of Spain Circular 2/2016** regulations
- Long-term variable incentives for executive directors and senior management are tied to diversity metrics (e.g., evolution of women in management positions accounts for 5% of long-term variable remuneration)

### **7. Current Leadership Structure**

BBVA's published senior leadership includes:
- **Executive Chairman**: Carlos Torres Vila
- **CEO**: Onur Genç
- **CFO**: Gonzalo Rodríguez Rodríguez
- **CCO (Chief Compliance Officer)**: Rocío Pérez Mies
- **CRO (Chief Risk Officer)**: Pablo Pastor / José Luis Elechiguerra
- **Country Manager, BBVA Spain**: Cristina de Parias
- **Global Head of Talent & Culture**: Paul G. Tobin

### **8. Career Opportunities & Recruitment**

BBVA emphasizes talent and culture as strategic priorities:
- Career opportunities are posted on **bbva.com** and through dedicated careers channels
- The bank offers global mobility across Spain, Latin America, Turkey, the US, and Asia
- Focus on innovation, digital banking, AI, and fintech attracts professionals in these fields
- BBVA was recognized among the **10 best companies in the world** by Time magazine's "World's Best Companies 2025"

These published requirements demonstrate BBVA's commitment to transparency in leadership selection, with clear emphasis on professional qualifications, diversity, regulatory compliance, and alignment with the bank's digital transformation and sustainability strategies.

answer:
Based on the latest available data from the European Banking Authority (EBA) Risk Dashboard for Q4 2025 (published in March 2026), the average financial metrics for EU/EEA banks are:

**CET1 Capital Ratio:** Approximately **15.8–16.0%** (near record levels)

**NPL Ratio:** **1.8%**

These figures demonstrate that EU banks maintain a robust capital position with capital ratios at near-record levels, driven by strong organic capital growth. The non-performing loan ratio has remained stable at 1.8%, with NPL volumes at approximately €370 billion in Q4 2025.

Additional context:
- Under full CRR3 implementation, the average CET1 ratio is projected to decline slightly to 15.3%, while remaining robust
- The share of Stage 2 loans fell to 9.1% in Q4 2025, indicating improving credit quality
- The ECB noted that overall CET1 requirements and guidance applicable in 2026 are steady at 11.2%, meaning EU/EEA banks hold substantial buffers above minimum requirements

Note: Q4 2025 represents the most recent publicly available data from the EBA Risk Dashboard as of the information provided.

query: What capital and liquidity (LCR) levels do significant institutions supervised by the ECB report?
answer:
Significant institutions supervised by the European Central Bank (ECB) report strong capital and liquidity levels that are well above regulatory minimums.

## Capital Ratios (Q2 2025)

Based on the most recent published data for the second quarter of 2025:

- **Common Equity Tier 1 (CET1) ratio: 16.12%** – up from 16.05% in Q1 2025 and 15.81% one year earlier
- **Tier 1 ratio: 17.60%**
- **Total Capital ratio: 20.24%** – slightly down from 20.29% in Q1 2025

The CET1 ratio varies significantly across countries, ranging from **13.18% in Spain to 23.71% in Latvia** in Q2 2025.

These capital levels provide substantial headroom above regulatory requirements. The overall SREP (Supervisory Review and Evaluation Process) CET1 requirements and guidance, including systemic and countercyclical buffers, stood at approximately **11.7%** as of the 2019 SREP cycle. CET1 ratios have reached new highs, further increasing capital headroom and contributing to banking sector resilience.

## Liquidity Coverage Ratio (LCR)

- **Aggregate LCR: 157.84%** in Q2 2025, up from 156.24% in Q1 2025

This is well above the regulatory minimum of **100%**. The European Banking Authority's June 2026 Risk Assessment Report expects the sector's LCR to decline modestly to about **155% in 2026**, while remaining comfortably above the minimum requirement.

The ECB publishes these aggregated supervisory banking statistics on a quarterly basis, drawing on harmonized COREP (common reporting) and FINREP (financial reporting) frameworks from banks it directly supervises.

## Capital and Liquidity Levels of ECB-Supervised Significant Institutions

The European Central Bank publishes aggregate supervisory banking statistics on significant institutions (SIs) — the banks it directly supervises — on a quarterly basis, drawing on harmonised COREP and FINREP reporting frameworks.

### Capital Ratios

Based on the most recent published data (Q2 2025, released 17 September 2025):

- **Aggregate CET1 (Common Equity Tier 1) ratio: 16.12%** — up from 16.05% in Q1 2025 and 15.81% a year earlier.
- **Aggregate Tier 1 ratio: 17.60%**
- **Aggregate Total Capital ratio: 20.24%** — slightly down from 20.29% in Q1 2025.

Across countries, the CET1 ratio ranged from **13.18% in Spain to 23.71% in Latvia** in Q2 2025.

For context, the overall SREP CET1 requirements and guidance (including systemic and countercyclical buffers) requested by authorities stood at approximately **11.7%** as of the 2019 SREP cycle, meaning the sector maintains substantial headroom above regulatory minimums. CET1 ratios have been described as reaching a new high, further increasing capital headroom and contributing to banking sector resilience.

### Liquidity Coverage Ratio (LCR)

- **Aggregate LCR: 157.84%** in Q2 2025, up from 156.24% in Q1 2025.

This is well above the regulatory minimum of **100%**. The EBA's June 2026 Risk Assessment Report expects the sector's LCR to decline modestly to about **155% in 2026**, while remaining comfortably above the minimum.

### Key Takeaways

- Euro area significant institutions hold capital and liquidity buffers significantly above regulatory minimums.
- Capital ratios have been on an upward trend, with CET1 reaching new highs.
- The LCR remains robust at roughly 155–158%, providing ample short-term liquidity coverage.
- The ECB publishes updated supervisory banking statistics quarterly via its Data Portal, with the next update expected to cover more recent quarters.

query: What has been the trend of Spain's GDP, inflation (HICP) and unemployment in recent years?
answer:
Spain's economy has shown strong positive trends across key macroeconomic indicators in recent years:

## GDP Growth

Spain has been the standout performer among major eurozone economies:

- **2023:** Spain significantly outpaced eurozone peers (which grew just 0.4%)
- **2024:** GDP growth was revised upward, with robust expansion far exceeding the eurozone's 0.9%
- **2025:** The economy grew **2.8%** for the full year—more than double the eurozone average of 1.5%. Quarter-on-quarter growth was 0.8% in Q2 and 0.6% in Q3. Spain's total output has risen approximately 10% since 2019, well above the eurozone average of 6.4%
- **2026 forecast:** GDP growth is expected at around **2.1%**, still well above the eurozone average

Key growth drivers include record tourism (approximately 97 million international visitors in 2025), strong immigration fueling labor supply and consumption, low energy costs, rising exports, and dynamic non-tourism services (IT, telecoms, business services). All three major rating agencies—S&P, Moody's, and Fitch—upgraded Spain's sovereign credit rating in September 2025, citing improved economic resilience and balanced growth.

## Inflation (HICP)

Spain's EU-harmonized inflation (HICP) has shown mixed trends:

- Spain's HICP was among the lowest in the eurozone for much of 2024–2025, helped by relatively low energy prices
- By **October 2025**, HICP had risen to **3.2%** year-on-year (up from 3.0% in September), above the 3.0% analysts had expected
- Core inflation stood at **2.5%** in October 2025
- **Industrial prices** surged in early 2026: in **April 2026**, Spanish industrial prices rose **8.3% year-on-year**—the fastest since December 2022—driven mainly by oil refining and chemicals costs, posing an upside risk to consumer inflation

## Unemployment

Spain's unemployment rate remains the highest in the EU but has been on a clear downward trend:

- **Q3 2025:** 10.45%
- **Q4 2025:** **9.93%**—falling below 10% for the first time in years
- **2026 forecast:** approximately **9.8%**

More than half of jobs created since 2020 have been filled by immigrant workers. The 2021 labor reform boosted permanent contracts: in tourism alone, 91.9% of new jobs in 2025 were permanent, and the temporary employment rate fell to 7.6%.

## Summary

Spain's economy is in a strong cyclical position—leading European growth, receiving credit upgrades, and seeing falling unemployment. However, challenges remain: inflation pressures are re-emerging (especially from industrial/energy costs), unemployment is still the EU's highest, housing costs surged nearly 13% in 2025, and GDP per capita gains lag behind headline growth due to immigration-driven population expansion.

## Spain Unemployment Rate — Recent Trend

Spain's unemployment rate has been on a **steady downward trajectory** in recent years, continuing a recovery that began after the pandemic peak:

| Year | Annual Unemployment Rate |
|------|------------------------|
| 2022 | ~13.0% |
| 2023 | **12.18%** |
| 2024 | **11.40%** |
| 2025 | **10.38%** |
| 2026 (YTD) | **~10.2%** |

### Key takeaways

- **Consistent year-over-year declines**: The rate fell roughly 0.8–1.0 percentage points each year from 2023 through 2025.
- **Latest reading**: As of March 2026, the overall unemployment rate stood at approximately **10.3%**, marking the lowest level in many years.
- **Monthly pattern in 2025**: The rate ranged from about 9.7% (for those over 24) at the start of the year down to 9.0% by December 2025, reflecting seasonal and structural improvements.
- **Youth unemployment remains elevated**: The under-25 unemployment rate was around **23.8%** as of early 2026 — still high but also trending down from 26.3% at the start of 2025.

Despite remaining one of the higher unemployment rates in the EU, Spain has made significant progress, with the overall rate declining from above 13% in 2022 to roughly 10% in 2026.

The statement that the rate fell roughly 0.8–1.0 percentage points each year is supported by the year‑over‑year declines shown in the same fact (0.85% from 2022‑2023, 0.78% from 2023‑2024, 1.02% from 2024‑2025, and 0.14% from 2025‑2026).
The latest reading of about 10.3% in March 2026 comes from the Statista fact that records the unemployment rate as 10.3% for March 2026.
The youth unemployment figure of roughly 23.8% in early 2026 is corroborated by the age‑specific data fact showing under‑25 unemployment at 23.8% for 2026.

The monthly pattern in 2025, with the overall rate moving from about 9.7% in January to 9.0% in December, is supported by the 2025 monthly breakdown fact that lists the over‑24 rate for each month (e.g., 9.7% in January, 9.0% in December).

{"content":"## Spain HICP Inflation Trend — Recent Years

Spain's Harmonised Index of Consumer Prices (HICP) has followed a notable trajectory over recent years:

### 2022–2023: Sharp disinflation
After peaking during the 2022 energy crisis, Spain's HICP inflation fell significantly through 2023 as energy prices normalised. By late 2023, the annual HICP rate had come down to around the 3% area (the eurozone-wide headline was at 3.3% in September 2023).

### 2024–2025: Moderate but persistent inflation
- Through much of 2024 and into 2025, Spain's HICP hovered around the **2.5–3.2%** range, remaining above the ECB's 2% target.
- In **October 2025**, Spain's EU-harmonised 12-month inflation rose to **3.2%**, up from 3.0% in September, exceeding the 3.0% analyst consensus. Core inflation (excluding fresh food and energy) stood at **2.5%** year-on-year.

### 2026: Re-acceleration driven by energy
- Inflation has picked up again in 2026, largely driven by surging energy prices (linked in part to geopolitical tensions, including the Iran/Hormuz situation).
- Spain's **industrial prices** rose **8.3% year-on-year in April 2026**, the fastest pace since December 2022, mainly driven by oil refining and chemicals — a leading indicator of consumer price pressures.
- By **August 2026**, eurozone-wide headline HICP hit **3.3%** (the highest since September 2023), with energy inflation at 14.3% year-on-year. Within that, **Spain recorded a 12-month HICP rate of 4.5%** — the highest among the Big Four eurozone economies. Spain's three-month annualised HICP pace reached **7.0%**, though the core rate was more contained at **2.9%** over 12 months and **2.6%** over three months.

### Key takeaway
Spain's HICP inflation followed a disinflationary path from the 2022 peak through 2023–2024, but has re-accelerated in 2025–2026. Energy costs are the primary driver of the latest surge, while core inflation remains elevated but more moderate. Spain currently runs above the eurozone average, partly reflecting strong domestic demand, a booming tourism sector, and pass-through from higher industrial input costs.

There's a good deal of concern about the development of inflation globally and across individual areas where central banks are making decisions on what to do with policy. In the euro area in August, the headline rate rose by 0.4%, with the core rising by just 0.2%. The three-month inflation rate for headline HICP inflation is 3.3% annualized while the pace for the core is only 2.4% annualized. ## Spain HICP Inflation Trend — Recent Years

Spain's Harmonised Index of Consumer Prices (HICP) has followed a notable trajectory over recent years:

### 2022–2023: Sharp disinflation
After peaking during the 2022 energy crisis, Spain's HICP inflation fell significantly through 2023 as energy prices normalised. By late 2023, the annual HICP rate had come down to around the 3% area (the eurozone-wide headline was at 3.3% in September 2023).

### 2024–2025: Moderate but persistent inflation
- Through much of 2024 and into 2025, Spain's HICP hovered around the **2.5–3.2%** range, remaining above the ECB's 2% target.
- In **October 2025**, Spain's EU-harmonised 12-month inflation rose to **3.2%**, up from 3.0% in September, exceeding the 3.0% analyst consensus. Core inflation (excluding fresh food and energy) stood at **2.5%** year-on-year.

### 2026: Re-acceleration driven by energy
- Inflation has picked up again in 2026, largely driven by surging energy prices (linked in part to geopolitical tensions, including the Iran/Hormuz situation).
- Spain's **industrial prices** rose **8.3% year-on-year in April 2026**, the fastest pace since December 2022, mainly driven by oil refining and chemicals — a leading indicator of consumer price pressures.
- By **August 2026**, eurozone-wide headline HICP hit **3.3%** (the highest since September 2023), with energy inflation at 14.3% year-on-year. Within that, **Spain recorded a 12-month HICP rate of 4.5%** — the highest among the Big Four eurozone economies. Spain's three-month annualised HICP pace reached **7.0%**, though the core rate was more contained at **2.9%** over 12 months and **2.6%** over three months.

### Key takeaway
Spain's HICP inflation followed a disinflationary path from the 2022 peak through 2023–2024, but has re-accelerated in 2025–2026. Energy costs are the primary driver of the latest surge, while core inflation remains elevated but more moderate. Spain currently runs above the eurozone average, partly reflecting strong domestic demand, a booming tourism sector, and pass-through from higher industrial input costs.

*Latest data referenced: August 2026 (Eurostat flash estimate / Haver Analytics, published 1 September 2026).*

# EMU Inflation Is Too High but Not Jet-setting

by:Robert Brusca

|in:Economy in Brief

There's a good deal of concern about the development of inflation globally and across individual areas where central banks are making decisions on what to do with policy. In the euro area in August, the headline rate rose by 0.4%, with the core rising by just 0.2%. The three-month inflation rate for headline HICP inflation is 3.3% annualized while the pace for the core is only 2.4% annualized. That's excessive relative to the 2% target but not a particularly strong acceleration for inflation. It's not the kind of number that says to the ECB that it has to raise rates right now. [...] The Big Four economies in the monetary union all have year-over-year inflation rates for the headline that are excessive compared to the target set for the entire community. France has the lowest 12-month headline pace at 2.7%. Spain has the highest at 4.5%. Over three months, both France and Italy run headline inflation near a pace of 1.5%, while German inflation runs hot at 3.7% and Spanish inflation sizzles at a 7.0% pace.

Once again, however, core is a better-behaved series, at a 12-month pace of 2.9% for Spain, 1.4% for Italy, and with German ex-energy inflation up at a 12-month pace of 2.2%. # Eurozone Inflation Hits 3.3%: What It Means for the ECB Hike, Bunds and the Euro

Euro area flash HICP inflation printed 3.3% year on year in August 2026, up from 2.9% in July and matching the consensus, according to Eurostat’s estimate released on Tuesday morning. Energy inflation accelerated to 14.3% from 10.3%, while core inflation — excluding energy, food, alcohol and tobacco — eased to 2.4% from 2.5%. Markets had already treated a 25-basis-point European Central Bank rise on 10 September as all but certain; the headline print leaves that path intact and keeps German Bund yields near multi-year highs. [...] The bear case is that energy stays expensive into winter, unprocessed food picks up further, and services stop falling. Headline HICP would then stay well above 2% into 2027, forcing the Council to treat 2.50% as a waypoint rather than a destination. Bund yields would push through the recent highs, EUR could catch a policy bid versus lower-yielding currencies even as European equities suffer from tighter financial conditions, and credit spreads would widen. Persistent Hormuz disruption that keeps Brent in a high range is the main external fuel for that path.

What Happens Next

A short list will decide whether 3.3% was confirmation or the start of a harder cycle: [...] What Happened?

Eurostat’s flash estimate put all-items HICP at 3.3% in August, after 2.9% in July. Month on month, the index rose 0.4%. That is the highest annual rate since September 2023. Energy was the dominant driver at 14.3% year on year, after 10.3% in July, and rose 2.9% on the month alone. Food, alcohol and tobacco held at 1.2%. Non-energy industrial goods picked up to 1.2% from 0.9%. Services — the component the ECB watches most closely for persistence — slowed to 3.0% from 3.3%.

Spain is the **4th-largest economy in the EU** and the **15th-largest globally**, with a GDP of approximately **$1.72 trillion**. Over recent years, Spain has consistently outperformed its eurozone peers in economic growth:

### Key Growth Drivers

- **Tourism**: 2025 was a record year — nearly 97 million overseas visitors, with tourism contributing €218.5 billion (13% of GDP).
- **Immigration & labour market**: More than half of jobs created since 2020 were filled by immigrants, boosting overall output. Unemployment has fallen to ~10.5%.
- **Non-tourism services**: Business, telecoms, and IT services have diversified Spain's growth beyond traditional sectors.
- **Low energy costs & competitiveness**: Moderate wage growth and relatively low energy prices have strengthened external competitiveness.

## Spain GDP Trend — Recent Years

Spain is the **4th-largest economy in the EU** and the **15th-largest globally**, with a GDP of approximately **$1.72 trillion**. Over recent years, Spain has consistently outperformed its eurozone peers in economic growth:

### Annual GDP Growth

| Year | GDP Growth (%) | Key Context |
|------|---------------|-------------|
| **2023** | ~2.7% | Strong post-pandemic rebound; tourism surged (+10.5% in tourism GDP) |
| **2024** | ~2.8% | Fuelled by consumer demand, rising exports, and robust tourism (+5.5% tourism GDP growth) |
| **2025** | **2.8%** | Government and Bank of Spain forecast 2.7–2.9%; more than double the eurozone average of ~1.2% |
| **2026 (forecast)** | **~2.1–2.2%** | Q1 2026 came in at 2.7% YoY; Q2 2026 at 0.7% quarter-on-quarter — still the fastest among large eurozone economies |

### Key Growth Drivers

- **Tourism**: 2025 was a record year — nearly 97 million overseas visitors, with tourism contributing €218.5 billion (13% of GDP).
- **Immigration & labour market**: More than half of jobs created since 2020 were filled by immigrants, boosting overall output. Unemployment has fallen to ~10.5%.
- **Non-tourism services**: Business, telecoms, and IT services have diversified Spain's growth beyond traditional sectors.
- **Low energy costs & competitiveness**: Moderate wage growth and relatively low energy prices have strengthened external competitiveness.

### Credit Rating Upgrades

In September 2025, Spain received a **triple credit rating upgrade** from all three major agencies:
- **S&P Global**: Cited "notable improvement" in Spain's balance sheet
- **Moody's**: Upgraded to A3, citing economic strength and banking sector resilience
- **Fitch**: Upgraded to A, highlighting productivity gains and external competitiveness

### Caveats

- Spain's GDP output has risen **10% since 2019**, well above the eurozone average of 6.4%. However, much of this growth is driven by population expansion through immigration, meaning **GDP per capita has advanced less strongly**.
- Unemployment at ~10.5% remains the **highest in the EU**.
- Industrial prices rose 8.3% year-on-year in April 2026, and inflation climbed to 3.5–3.6% by mid-2026, posing a potential headwind.

Overall, Spain has been the **standout growth story** in the eurozone since 2021, though analysts note the growth model is more "extensive" (population-driven) than "intensive" (productivity-driven).
